title: Full f41r target localization succeeds but pixel-width foot criteria remain mostly unresolved
statement: The f41r narrow target670,403,706,450 omitted left-stroke/base context; the full neighborhood630,390,735,480 retains both stems and the complete basal region. Paired model rereads with source labels withheld now localize the complete two-stem graphic in all7 contexts, including the open-upper-return f41r example. A new frozen operational foot rule requires an isolated outward extension at least as wide as the local right-stem shaft, using manual native-pixel uncertainty intervals. Independent computation from each reader output agrees in category for all7 contexts: f104r and control f46r present, the other5 unclear. No reported/computed-rule mismatch occurs. Both positive contexts meet the threshold only at equality; a post-review one-pixel-margin sensitivity makes both unclear. This is localization and measurement-method progress, not validated metrology or hand3 identification.

localization.correction: Earlier rejection concerned a partly framed fragment, not a demonstrated absence of K on the page. Wider context shows both stems. Transcript line3 aligns a k-bearing word in ZL/IT/RF; this supports glyph identity/location only, not detailed morphology or handwriting attribution.

criterion.target: Outward rightward projection at the base of the right stem, separate from stem thickening and following-letter ink.
criterion.width: Estimate an interval in native pixels for local shaft width from3 cross-sections of a clear lower straight stem segment before the basal bend. If boundaries/axis cannot be identified, report null.
criterion.extension: Estimate an interval for rightward extent beyond the continuation of the shaft right edge at the base; exclude ordinary shaft thickness. Native pixels only. If ownership or stroke direction cannot be separated, report null.
criterion.present: Base fully visible, isolated from neighboring ink by a visible paper gap, and extension lower bound >= shaft-width upper bound.
criterion.absent: Base fully visible and isolated, extension upper bound < shaft-width lower bound.
criterion.unclear: Missing/cropped/overlapping base, unknown shaft or extension, threshold-straddling intervals, or unaccepted target. Do not force rounding at a one-pixel boundary.

check: Keep the corrected full-glyph localization and explicit stroke-membership requirements. Before using the foot rule diagnostically, validate pixel-boundary estimates and threshold robustness on known-script examples with expert-marked contours. Obtain matched-context specimens and treat threshold-straddling estimates as unclear. Do not reuse old subjective foot labels as if they were measured by the new definition, or convert high abstention agreement into handwriting accuracy.

protocol.scope: Correct f41r target localization and prospectively apply a new explicit right-stem basal-projection rule to all7 prior K contexts. Original annotations and earlier rereads are retained. This is method development after prior outcomes, not confirmation.
protocol.localization: Previous f41r target670,403,706,450 was narrower than the glyph neighborhood and could omit left-stroke ink. Full contextual cut630,390,735,480 retains both sides and baseline with margin. ZL/IT/RF line3 all record a k-bearing third word, with different initial readings; transcript alignment supports identity/location only, not fine geometry or hand attribution.

projection_rule.target: Outward rightward projection at the base of the right stem, separate from stem thickening and following-letter ink.
projection_rule.width: Estimate an interval in native pixels for local shaft width from3 cross-sections of a clear lower straight stem segment before the basal bend. If boundaries/axis cannot be identified, report null.
projection_rule.extension: Estimate an interval for rightward extent beyond the continuation of the shaft right edge at the base; exclude ordinary shaft thickness. Native pixels only. If ownership or stroke direction cannot be separated, report null.
projection_rule.present: Base fully visible, isolated from neighboring ink by a visible paper gap, and extension lower bound >= shaft-width upper bound.
projection_rule.absent: Base fully visible and isolated, extension upper bound < shaft-width lower bound.
projection_rule.unclear: Missing/cropped/overlapping base, unknown shaft or extension, threshold-straddling intervals, or unaccepted target. Do not force rounding at a one-pixel boundary.

protocol.review: Same two masked model readers, all7 contexts, new shuffled codes, source labels and other-reader outputs withheld. Arrows locate the full intended form; a zoom window is not a glyph segmentation boundary. Native TIFF where available; no sharpening/binarization. Native dimensions and 6x display shown.
protocol.analysis: Freeze both new files before source-linked comparison. Derive rule category independently from reported intervals and flags, retaining reported category and inconsistencies. Report abstentions and cross-reader interval overlap. Never overwrite older subjective foot ratings or claim attribution accuracy.
protocol.limitations: Pixel intervals are manual model estimates, not instrument measurements or validated paleographic criteria. Reader memory, root-known labels and selected prior contexts remain. This rule is exploratory and conservative, and cannot reconstruct pen order.

analysis_plan.rule: Independently derive present/absent/unclear from each reader interval and localization/visibility flags. Retain reported-category mismatches, all7 cases and abstentions. Compare only categories under the same new rule, not nominal earlier foot labels as if unchanged. No p-values or attribution inference.
analysis_plan.freeze: Hash both final7-row files before source-linked analysis; initial ratings and previous review remain unchanged.

A.note: Both stems and the full base are visible. The right shaft narrows and slopes slightly before a small outward basal wedge. Three straight lower sections suggest about 3–5 native pixels of width; soft boundaries and extrapolation of the right edge give about 2–5 pixels of lateral extension. Paper separates the base from the next glyph, but the size comparison overlaps.

B.note: The complete paired form and paper around its right base are visible. Three lower straight-shaft sections around local y55,60,65 support roughly 4-6 native pixels of width. A short rightward basal spur extends roughly 4-7 pixels beyond the continued shaft edge. The soft boundaries and modest shaft slant make those intervals overlap the rule threshold; neither inequality is established.

A.note: The complete paired stems are identifiable in context. Three lower straight-shaft cross-sections give an approximate 3–5 native-pixel width. The right stem widens rightward at its base, with paper before the next glyph; continuation of its sloping, softly bounded right edge gives roughly 2–6 pixels of extension. The intervals do not establish either inequality.

B.note: Both stems and the complete right basal ending can be followed in context. Three right-shaft sections around local y45,50,55 support a width of roughly 3-5 pixels. The base broadens rightward beyond the continued edge by about 2-5 pixels. Paper separates it from the next glyph, but blur and the gradual widening leave extension and shaft-width intervals overlapping.

A.note: The two-stem graphic is localized despite the stroke approaching from above. Three lower straight-shaft sections indicate roughly 3–5 native pixels. A small rightward wedge appears at the base, separated from the next glyph by paper; its extent beyond the continued sloping shaft edge is approximately 2–5 pixels. The projection-to-width comparison remains unresolved.

B.note: The right stem is fully visible and separated from the following letter. Three lower straight sections around local y45,50,55 support roughly 4-6 pixels of width. Its terminal wedge extends only about 1-4 pixels beyond the continued right edge; most of the dark base remains within the shaft's continuation. The boundary uncertainty reaches the absent threshold, preventing a strict less-than decision.

A.note: The right stem is relatively thin through three lower straight cross-sections, approximately 2–4 native pixels wide. At its base an identifiable rising rightward extension reaches about 4–7 pixels beyond the continued shaft edge and stops before a paper gap to the following glyph. The lower extension bound meets the upper shaft-width bound.

B.note: The right stem slopes down-left before turning outward to the right. Three straight portions around local y50,55,60 give approximately 3-5 pixels of width. Continuing that slanted right edge to the basal turn leaves about 5-8 pixels of outward extension. Paper separates the short tip from the next letter. The extension lower bound reaches the shaft-width upper bound.

A.note: The open upper return does not prevent localizing both stems. Three lower straight sections of the right stem suggest roughly 4–6 native pixels of width. Its blunt basal swelling is separated from neighboring ink, but extrapolating the right shaft edge gives only an uncertain 0–4-pixel excess. A rounded ending and a small extension cannot be separated securely; the intervals meet at a boundary rather than proving absence.

B.note: The upper-right return has a visible opening, while the complete two-stem graphic is still localizable. Lower straight sections around local y50,55,60 give approximately 4-6 pixels of shaft width. A small rightward basal bulge projects about 2-5 pixels beyond the continued edge. The base is complete and separate from adjacent ink, but the intervals satisfy neither category inequality.

A.note: The target has two complete stems. Three straight sections before the right stem bends suggest about 3–5 native pixels of shaft width. Its basal rightward projection reaches approximately 5–9 pixels beyond the continued sloping right edge, with clear paper before the following ink. This meets the specified projection threshold, allowing for the soft pixel boundary.

B.note: The complete paired form has a right shaft slanting down-left, then a distinct outward basal curl. Three pre-bend sections around local y55,60,65 indicate approximately 3-5 pixels of width. Relative to continuation of that slanted right edge, the curl extends about 5-9 native pixels rightward. A paper gap separates its tip from the following letter. The extension lower bound reaches the shaft-width upper bound.

A.note: The full graphic has two visible stems connected below an open upper hook. Three lower straight right-shaft sections suggest approximately 2–4 native pixels. The fully visible base is separated from the following ink by paper, but its slight rounded widening gives about 0–3 pixels beyond the continued shaft edge. The intervals overlap, so the explicit rule does not resolve the category.

B.note: Context localizes both stems despite the open upper hook. Sections around local y45,50,55 suggest a 3-5 pixel right shaft. Its lower ending is mostly a taper or rounded thickening; a possible outward excess is only about 0-3 pixels, with soft boundaries. The upper extension bound meets the lower width bound, so the strict absent inequality is not satisfied. Neighboring ink is separated by paper.

one_pixel_sensitivity.timing: Post-review descriptive sensitivity after noticing positive margins equal0. Does not replace the frozen >= primary rule or revise annotations.
one_pixel_sensitivity.change: Require extension lower bound >= shaft-width upper bound +1 native pixel for present; all other primary gates unchanged.

limitations: The same two model readers return manual pixel intervals; these are visual estimates, not measured contours or instrument-validated confidence bounds. Shared model and previous-image memory remain.

This is an exploratory operational criterion declared after earlier foot disagreements. It tests a new definition; nominal comparison with old present/absent labels is not a confirmatory accuracy comparison.
Five of7 categories are jointly unclear. Agreement of7/7 therefore must be reported with only2 jointly resolved contexts, and those2 are threshold-boundary positives.
All7 images now use original TIFF at the same native dimensions as the JPEG views.6x nearest-neighbor display and rulers do not add optical resolution or recover missing ink.

The accepted object is the complete localized two-stem graphic; an open upper return is not automatically rejected as in the narrow-frame interpretation. This is not a new expert alphabet/hand attribution.
The7 selected examples are not a complete glyph census, independent bifolios or new readers. No hidden-page data, seed, fact or classifier verdict was used.

reader_provenance.A: Same /root/masked_reader_a,7 final annotations, no procedural deviations reported.
reader_provenance.B: Same /root/masked_reader_b,7 final annotations, no procedural deviations reported.
reader_provenance.masking: New shuffled card IDs, no folio/hand labels, transcripts or other-reader outputs supplied. Root knows mapping. This is a paired followup, not fresh independent replication.

reproduction.usage: Decode files_base64 preserving exact bytes and relative folder names under a clean root; run python k-localization/analyze.py. No source TIFF needed to recompute ratings/rule metrics. To regenerate image cards, download TIFF URLs and verify hashes in tiff-sources.json; adjust local path fields to those files and restore prior review-key/detail-boxes from PR650/PR645 for prepare.py. The embedded final card hashes and annotation hashes are the audit record; do not overwrite them after a rerender.
